headline: Intel, AMD and Nvidia showed new AI data-centre chips, server racks and software at the Open Compute Project summit in Silicon Valley.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a round-up of company announcements, mostly roadmap claims.
importance_line: It affects data-centre builders and their customers who want alternatives to Nvidia, and the performance numbers are the companies' own.
summary: CRN reports that at the OCP Global Summit (run by the Open Compute Project, the data-centre hardware group founded by Meta), Intel said its 480 GB air-cooled "Crescent Island" AI inference chip, now sampling with customers, will be sold as the Intel GPU D-series, AMD unveiled a flexible "Helion" server rack design and a 192-core EPYC chip called Verano due in production in the first half of 2027, and Nvidia open-sourced data-centre software including Run:ai. CRN's own spec comparison puts Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000 ahead of Intel's card on 8-bit speed, while Intel's card carries far more memory.
